title: Ops shift rotation debrief — GPU on-call week 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-30
content:
Summary:
This note captures the on-call handoffs, incidents, and operational observations from the GPU fleet on-call rotation covering 2026-09-23 to 2026-09-30. Focus areas: cross-region surge during APAC morning peak, two short NVMe node degradations in eu-west, and a recurring QoS throttling pattern tied to a background snapshot job.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-09-24 02:10 UTC — APAC burst: unexpected spike in hosted API small-chat endpoints bumped queue depth in ap-southeast-1. Smart-routing handed off 12% of traffic to dedicated pool; latency climbed from 120ms -> 340ms for 6 minutes. No data loss.
- 2026-09-25 11:40 UTC — eu-west NVMe: degraded disks on 3 nodes in cluster gpu-eu-3, pods evicted and rescheduled across remainder of cluster. Evictions lasted ~18 minutes, autoscaler filled 2 of 3 slots with preemptible instances.
- 2026-09-27 23:00 UTC — Snapshot job overlap: quarterly snapshot job for dedicated customers overlapped with inference cache warm-up, causing repeated KV cache evictions and steady token throughput drop for ~40 minutes.
- Handovers completed each day between 08:00 UTC and 09:00 UTC with short notes pushed to the #gpu-ops channel.

Metrics snapshot (observed during incidents):
- 99th percentile token latency: baseline 210ms -> spike 420ms during APAC burst
- Eviction count (eu-west event): 31 pod evictions across 3 hosts
- Autoscaling fill time: average 9.2 minutes to steady-state after preemptible boots
- Snapshot overlap CPU pressure: dedicated-control plane CPU saturation observed at 78% (spike to 92%)

What went well:
- Smart-routing fallback worked as designed: the policy rerouted excess requests to dedicated capacity and degraded gracefully instead of erroring. Post-mortem shows the policy threshold caught traffic at ~85% saturation and applied the route rule within 20s.
- Eviction automation: evicted pods were rescheduled successfully; persistent volumes reattached without manual intervention. Recovery within SLA.
- On-call communication: handoffs consistently posted summarized bullet points to channel and updated status page. Engineers were reachable and escalation chain used correctly.

What could be improved / Root causes & notes:
- APAC spike origin unclear: initial traffic source looks like a customer A/B test (INFRA-2781) that rolled out in ap-southeast region with an aggressive fan-out. Need confirmation from CS/product before we finalize mitigation rules.
- Snapshot scheduling mismatch: quarterly snapshot job is still running on the same low-traffic windows we use for cache priming. The job is non-latency-sensitive and should be moved to a different maintenance window or rate-limited.
- NVMe health telemetry: disk SMART thresholds are conservative; nodes reported I/O latency but not explicit SMART failure until after partial degradation. Recommend adding earlier I/O anomaly alerts to avoid mass evictions.
- Autoscaler cold-fill time: cold start for preemptible instances remains a tail risk (9m median). For dedicated-critical pools we should look into burst-capacity warmers (small reserved pool) to reduce 9m to <3m.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- AI-1: Ask product/CS to pause INFRA-2781 test in ap-southeast-1 and provide traffic pattern. Owner: Evan Liu. ETA: 2026-10-01.
- AI-2: Move quarterly snapshot job to secondary maintenance window and add token bucket limiter to snapshot worker. Owner: Samira Khan. ETA: 2026-10-07.
- AI-3: Add NVMe I/O latency anomaly alert: new alert when sustained 95th I/O latency > 15ms for 10 minutes. Owner: Miguel Ortega. ETA: 2026-10-05.
- AI-4: Prototype a 10-node warm pool in ap-southeast-1 for rapid burst absorption (opt-in config per customer tier). Owner: Noah Patel. ETA: 2026-10-20 (design), 2026-11-03 (trial).
- AI-5: Update shift handoff template to include quick-run metrics snapshot (top-3 clusters by tail latency) and any running maintenance jobs. Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2026-10-02.

Small operational notes / quick wins: 
- Add a small note to the runbook reminding on-call to check scheduled snapshot jobs before high-risk releases.
- Temporary mitigation: set lower concurrency cap for small-chat hosted route in ap-southeast-1 until the A/B test completes (config toggle exists in the console).
- Replace an ambiguous page in the status dashboard that aggregated both autoscaler and preemptible fill metrics; separated views will help on-call spot fill lag sooner.

Open questions / follow-ups for next rotation:
- Was the INFRA-2781 rollout intentionally global? (Product confirmation required)
- Can we standardize a ‘staggered start’ for maintenance snapshots across regions to avoid cache warm-up collisions?
- What SLO delta do we accept for a 5–10 minute autoscaler cold start for low-tier customers vs. enterprise-tier customers?

Post-rotation notes for managers:
- Suggested trial of warm pool in one region (ap-southeast-1) to validate warm-start economics vs. cost of occasional latency spikes. If successful, expand to eu-west.
- Consider a quarterly review of background jobs (snapshot/backup/benchmarks) that may interfere with cache behavior; propose to include infra in the release cadence calendar for these jobs.

Appendix: Relevant links and logs
- APAC spike trace (internal link): traces/2026-09-24/apac-spike-02-10
- NVMe degraded node logs: logs/gpu-eu-3/2026-09-25/*
- Snapshot job run details (task id): JOB-SNAP-20260927-11
- Pager history: incident/INC-2026-09-24-A

Notes to self & friction points observed during handoffs (informal):
- Handoff notes often miss the quick metric snapshot; adding a short CLI command in the template to capture top-3 tail latencies would be handy.
- The on-call rota has repeated adjacent shifts for a few engineers next month; recommend rebalancing to avoid burnout.

If there's anything missing from this debrief that folks want added before publishing to Confluence, ping me and I'll fold it in.

-- Priya
